mainTopic: A parent's death right before a wedding: the order of חופה, feast days and אבילות; רב חסדא's water-on-the-meat limit; and the couple sleeping apart in mourning and נדה cases
overview: This עמוד finishes a ברייתא about a parent who died just before a wedding while the food was already prepared. The wedding goes first, then the seven feast days, and then the seven days of אבילות, and the couple sleeps apart the whole time. The גמרא limits this rule to the death of the חתן's father or the כלה's mother. רב חסדא limits it further to when water was already put on the meat. רבא and רב פפא add that a big city and a village each work differently, and רב אשי shows that רב חסדא's rule applies in a middle-sized town like מתא מחסיא. A ברייתא supports רב חסדא and adds rules about a כלה who became a נדה, about jewelry, and about not having the first relations on Friday or Saturday night. The 'sleep apart' line supports רבי יוחנן, who holds that private mourning practices still apply on a Festival. רבא limits the נדה rule to a couple who had not yet been together, and the גמרא debates whether that limit also covers mourning. The last challenge, from the word 'וכן', is answered on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The wedding comes first, then the feast, then the mourning
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the חתן does the בעילת מצוה, separates, keeps the seven days of feasting, and only then keeps the seven days of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he has the מצוה intercourse and separates, and keeps the seven days of the feast, and afterward keeps the seven days of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the previous עמוד keeps going and lays out the order of events when a parent died just before the wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the wedding goes ahead first, the חתן does the בעילת מצוה and then separates from his wife. The שבעת ימי המשתה come before the שבעת ימי אבילות, so the mourning is pushed off until the celebration is over.

keyTerms.meaning: The first marital union that completes the wedding
The seven days of wedding celebration

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the middle of a ברייתא that began on the previous עמוד. The case is a parent who died right before the wedding while the food was already prepared.

phrases.english: And he has the מצוה intercourse and then separates,
and he keeps the seven days of the feast,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹהֵג שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי אֲבֵילוּת.
phrases.english: and afterward he keeps the seven days of mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous עמוד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wedding and the seven feast days come first, and the seven mourning days follow.

steps.title: The couple sleeps apart, but the bride keeps her jewelry
steps.stepSummary: During all those days the חתן sleeps among the men and the כלה among the women, and the כלה is not kept from wearing jewelry for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: During all those days he sleeps among the men and she sleeps among the women. And we do not keep jewelry from the bride for all thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by giving two extra rules for the couple during this mixed time of joy and mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the couple separated after the בעילת מצוה, they sleep in separate groups so they won't come together during this time. Even so, the כלה may still wear her jewelry for thirty days, even though it is a time of mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: Those days: the feast days and the mourning days

steps.whatToRemember: The order is: חופה and בעילת מצוה, then seven feast days, then seven mourning days. The couple sleeps apart the whole time, and the כלה keeps her jewelry for thirty days.

phrases.english: And all those days,
phrases.notes: This means both the seven feast days and the seven mourning days.

phrases.english: he sleeps among the men
and she sleeps among the women.
And we do not keep jewelry from the bride
for all thirty days.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The couple sleeps apart through all those days, and the כלה may wear jewelry for thirty days.

steps.title: Only the groom's father or the bride's mother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the ברייתא: the rule applies only when the father of the חתן or the mother of the כלה died, because nobody else would do the work for them. In the opposite case, the rule does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is only when it is the groom's father or the bride's mother, since there is no one else who would go to the trouble for them. But the other way around, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly which deaths the ברייתא is talking about, and it narrows the rule down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father of the חתן and the mother of the כלה are the ones who do the work of preparing the wedding. If one of them dies, nobody else would go to that trouble again, so the wedding goes ahead now. If the groom's mother or the bride's father died, this special order is not used.

keyTerms.meaning: Who would go to the trouble for them

steps.confusionAlert: It is easy to think the rule covers any parent. The גמרא limits it to just these two parents.

phrases.english: And this is only the groom's father
or the bride's mother,
since there is no one who would go to the trouble for them.
But the opposite case, no.
phrases.notes: The opposite case means the groom's mother or the bride's father died.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדַוְקָא, אָבִיו שֶׁל חָתָן אוֹ אִמָּהּ שֶׁל כַּלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows down which deaths the ברייתא covers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא's order applies only when the groom's father or the bride's mother died.

steps.title: רב חסדא: only once water was put on the meat
steps.stepSummary: רפרם בר פפא quotes רב חסדא: the rule applies only if water was already put on the meat. If not, the meat can still be sold, so the wedding does not go first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: They taught this only when water was already put on the meat. But if water was not put on the meat, it can be sold.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a second limit to the ברייתא, based on whether the meat can still be sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for pushing off the mourning is so the prepared food is not lost. Once water is on the meat it can't be sold, so the loss is real. If the meat is still sellable, there is no loss, and the normal order of mourning returns.

keyTerms.meaning: Put water on the meat (started preparing it for cooking)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the whole rule rests on avoiding a loss of the food, so it depends on whether the meat can still be sold.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa said in the name of Rav Chisda:
They taught this only
when he put water on the meat,
phrases.notes: Once the meat is soaking to be cooked, nobody will buy it anymore.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא נָתַן מַיִם עַל גַּבֵּי בָּשָׂר — מִזְדַּבַּן.
phrases.english: but if he did not put water on the meat, it can be sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁנָּתַן מַיִם עַל גַּבֵּי בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another limit to the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wedding goes first only if water was already put on the meat; otherwise the meat is sold.

steps.title: רבא: in a big city the meat can always be sold
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that in a big city, even if water was put on the meat, it can still be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And in a big city, even if water was put on the meat, it can be sold.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds that in a big city, the water does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a big city there are many buyers, so even soaked meat can be sold. That means there is no loss, so the wedding does not go first in a city.

phrases.english: Rava said: And in a big city,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנָּתַן מַיִם עַל גַּבֵּי בָּשָׂר — מִזְדַּבַּן.
phrases.english: even though he put water on the meat, it can be sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב חסדא's rule does not decide things in a big city
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a big city the meat can be sold even after water was put on it.

steps.title: רב פפא: in a village the meat can never be sold
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that in a village, even if no water was put on the meat, it cannot be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: And in a village, even if water was not put on the meat, it cannot be sold.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the opposite side: in a small village, the water does not matter either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A village does not have enough buyers for so much meat, so it can't be sold even when it is fresh. Since the loss would happen anyway, the wedding goes first in a village.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: And in a village,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן מַיִם עַל גַּבֵּי בָּשָׂר —
phrases.english: even though he did not put water on the meat,
it cannot be sold.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a village the meat cannot be sold even without water on it.

steps.title: So where does רב חסדא's rule ever apply?
steps.stepSummary: After רבא and רב פפא, the גמרא asks: if the water doesn't matter in a city or a village, when does רב חסדא's rule ever come into play?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, how do you find a case for רב חסדא's rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's rule, since the last two statements seem to leave no place where it matters. This sets up רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a city the meat is always sellable, and in a village it never is. So the question of water on the meat never changes anything. That makes רב חסדא's statement look pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find a case for it?

phrases.english: But then, Rav Chisda's rule,
how can you find a case for it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא using רבא and רב פפא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A city is always sellable and a village is never sellable, so water on the meat never changes the outcome.

steps.title: רב אשי: an in-between town like מתא מחסיא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that רב חסדא's rule applies in a place like מתא מחסיא, which is too small to be a big city and too big to be a village.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: In a place like מתא מחסיא, which is outside the category of a big city and outside the category of a village.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge by pointing to a middle-sized town where רב חסדא's rule really does decide the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a town that is in between, fresh meat can be sold but soaked meat can't. So there, whether water was put on the meat decides whether the wedding goes first. This saves רב חסדא's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: Big city: the meat can always be sold. Village: it can never be sold. A middle town like מתא מחסיא: it depends on whether water was put on the meat, just like רב חסדא said.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כְּגוֹן מָתָא מַחְסֵיָא,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Such as Mata Mechasya,
which is outside the category of a big city,
phrases.notes: Literally 'it goes out of a city': it is too small to count as one.

phrases.english: and outside the category of a village.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כְּגוֹן מָתָא מַחְסֵיָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a middle case where the rule applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא's rule seemed to have no real case, since every place is either a city or a village.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a middle-sized town, the water on the meat decides whether it can be sold, so רב חסדא's rule applies there.

steps.title: A ברייתא matching רב חסדא: the wedding goes ahead before the mourning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes a case where the meat already had water put on it and a parent died. The wedding happens first, then the seven feast days, then the seven days of אבילות, and the couple sleeps apart the whole time.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that matches רב חסדא. Suppose the bread was baked, the animal slaughtered, the wine mixed, and water was put on the meat, and then the father of the groom or the mother of the bride died. They move the body into a room and bring the groom and bride to the חופה. He has the first marital relations, which are a מצוה, and then separates from her. He keeps the seven days of feasting and afterward the seven days of mourning. During all those days he sleeps among the men and his wife sleeps among the women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that describes exactly the case where רב חסדא said the wedding comes first: the food was ready and water was already on the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the rule only applies once water was put on the meat (step 4), because then the meat can no longer be sold and would go to waste. The ברייתא mentions that same detail, so it backs him up. It also spells out the order: חופה first, then שבעת ימי המשתה, then שבעת ימי אבילות, with the couple sleeping apart throughout.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
The first marital relations, which complete the marriage and are a מצוה
The seven days of wedding celebration

steps.confusionAlert: The order surprises people. The seven feast days come FIRST and the seven mourning days come AFTER, even though the parent died before the wedding.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא gives רב חסדא's condition (water on the meat) an early source, so it is not just his own idea.

phrases.english: A ברייתא was taught in line with רב חסדא:
If his bread was already baked
and his animal slaughtered, and his wine mixed with water,
and he had put water on the meat,
and the father of the groom died
or the mother of the bride —
they bring the dead body into a room,
and the groom and the bride to the חופה,
and he has the first marital relations, which are a מצוה, and then separates,
and he keeps the seven days of feasting,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹהֵג שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי אֲבֵילוּת.
phrases.english: and afterward he keeps the seven days of mourning.
And during all those days,
he sleeps among the men
and his wife sleeps among the women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אשי showed where רב חסדא's rule applies, the גמרא brings an early source that supports רב חסדא.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule that the wedding goes first only once water was put on the meat.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists 'ונתן מים על גבי בשר' as part of the case where the wedding goes first.

steps.title: More rules from the ברייתא: a נדה bride, jewelry, and Friday and Saturday nights
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. A couple also sleeps apart when the wife became a נדה. A mourning כלה is not stopped from wearing jewelry. A first marriage should not be consummated on ליל שבת or מוצאי שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, if a man's wife became a נדה, he sleeps among the men and she sleeps among the women. We do not keep jewelry away from the bride during all thirty days. Either way, he should not have the first relations on Friday night or on Saturday night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and adds a few related rules about the new couple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'sleep apart' rule is extended to a bride who became a נדה, so the couple will not come to sin. Even though the כלה is in mourning, she may still wear jewelry for the first thirty days so she stays attractive to her new husband. The last line limits when the first relations may take place.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her monthly period, when marital relations are forbidden
Thirty days, the longer mourning period
Here it means Friday night, the start of שבת

phrases.english: And similarly, one whose wife became a נדה —
he sleeps among the men
and she sleeps among the women.
And we do not keep jewelry away from the bride
for all thirty days.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ לֹא יִבְעוֹל,
phrases.english: Either way, he should not have the first relations,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְלֹא בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: not on Friday night and not on Saturday night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the rest of the same ברייתא, adding related rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדה bride sleeps apart from her husband. A mourning כלה may wear jewelry for thirty days. The first relations should not take place on Friday night or Saturday night.

steps.title: Sleeping apart supports רבי יוחנן: private mourning still applies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line 'he sleeps among the men' and shows that it supports רבי יוחנן. Even when there is no public אבילות, private mourning practices are still kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'He sleeps among the men and she sleeps among the women.' This supports רבי יוחנן, who said: even though they said there is no mourning on a Festival, private matters are still kept.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now analyzes the ברייתא. It picks out one line and shows that it proves a statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the seven feast days the couple does not keep public mourning, much like a Festival. Yet they still sleep apart, which is a private mourning practice. So the ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: private mourning applies even when public mourning does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Private matters, mourning practices that others don't see

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule in הלכות אבילות: even when public mourning is put off, private mourning practices are still kept.

phrases.english: The Master said:
He sleeps among the men
and she sleeps among the women,
this supports רבי יוחנן.
For רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ אֵין אֲבֵילוּת בַּמּוֹעֵד,
phrases.english: Even though they said there is no mourning on a Festival,
private matters he does keep.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: הוּא יָשֵׁן בֵּין הָאֲנָשִׁים וְהִיא יְשֵׁנָה בֵּין הַנָּשִׁים, מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא turns from quoting the ברייתא to analyzing it, starting with the 'sleep apart' line.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that private mourning applies even when public mourning is suspended.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's rule that the couple sleeps apart during the feast days.

steps.title: רבא limits the נדה rule to a couple who had not yet been together
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a נדה bride sleeps apart only if the marriage had not yet been consummated. If it had, she may sleep with her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף the son of רבא taught in the name of רבא: this was taught only when he had not yet had relations with her. But if he had, his wife sleeps with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the ברייתא's rule that a husband and his נדה wife must sleep apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the first relations, the groom's desire is very strong, so there is a real worry that he will sin. Once they have been together, that worry is smaller, so she may sleep in the same place as him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this when', which narrows an earlier rule
He had marital relations with her

steps.confusionAlert: Watch which case רבא is talking about. The next steps argue over whether his limit also covers the mourning case: step 13 challenges him from the mourning case, step 14 answers that he meant only the נדה case, and step 15 pushes back on that answer.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא supports רב חסדא: the wedding comes first, then the feast days, then אבילות, with the couple sleeping apart. That line also supports רבי יוחנן on private mourning. רבא limits the נדה rule to before the first relations.

phrases.english: רב יוסף the son of רבא taught publicly
in the name of רבא:
They only taught this when he had not yet had relations with her,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the ברייתא's rule about a wife who became a נדה.

phrases.english: but if he had, his wife sleeps with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא בָּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא keeps analyzing the ברייתא and now narrows its נדה rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדה bride must sleep apart only if the marriage had not yet been consummated. If it had, she may sleep with her husband.

steps.title: The mourning case already had relations, yet they sleep apart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא. In the mourning case of the ברייתא the couple already had relations, yet it still says he sleeps among the men and she sleeps among the women.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here we are dealing with a case where he already had relations, and the ברייתא still teaches: he sleeps among the men and she sleeps among the women!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's rule. It points to the mourning case, where the couple already had relations but must still sleep apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that once a couple has had relations, they no longer need to sleep apart. In the mourning case of the ברייתא, the wedding and first relations already happened before the mourning began. Even so, the ברייתא makes them sleep apart, which seems to contradict רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He had marital relations (here, the first relations of the marriage)
We are dealing with (this kind of case)

phrases.english: But here, where we are dealing with a case where he already had relations,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the mourning case in the ברייתא, where the couple married and had relations before the mourning started.

phrases.english: and it teaches: he sleeps among the men
and she sleeps among the women!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's rule from Step 12 using the mourning case from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a couple who already had relations may sleep together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the mourning case the couple already had relations, yet the ברייתא still requires them to sleep apart. That goes against רבא.

steps.title: רבא was only talking about the נדה case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא's rule was said only about a bride who became a נדה, not about mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he said it, he was talking about a case where his wife became a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by limiting his rule. He only meant the case of a bride who became a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's leniency applies only to the נדה case. Mourning is a separate case with its own strictness, so there the couple sleeps apart even though they already had relations.

keyTerms.meaning: When he said it (he was referring to...)
She became a נדה (began her period)

phrases.english: When he said it, it was about a case where his wife became a נדה.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבא. His rule was only about the נדה case, not about mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13 by limiting רבא's rule to the נדה case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule (אוקימתא of רבא's statement)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבא's rule covered every case where they must sleep apart, mourning included.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's rule covers only the נדה case. Mourning keeps its own stricter rule.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says 'and likewise'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. The ברייתא connects the נדה case to the mourning case with the word 'וכן' ('and likewise'), which suggests they follow the same rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. The word 'וכן' seems to tie the נדה case and the mourning case together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 split the two cases apart: mourning is strict and נדה is lenient. But the ברייתא says 'and likewise' when it moves from mourning to נדה, which suggests the two cases are the same. If they are the same, רבא's distinction should apply to both or to neither.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise (it signals that two cases are the same)

steps.confusionAlert: 'וכן' is not just a connecting word here. The גמרא reads it as a sign that the two cases share the same law. That is the whole basis of the challenge.

phrases.english: But it teaches "and likewise"!
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא in Step 10: "and likewise" one whose wife became a נדה sleeps apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 14 using the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבא's rule covers only the נדה case and not mourning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'and likewise', which links the נדה case to the mourning case. So the two cases should not have different rules.
